title: Hand-pulled Smoked Chinese lamb Bao
description: A Xinjiang-inspired dish featuring smoky lamb, crispy bao, and tangy apple cider vinegar.
instructions: Rinse the lamb shoulder and pat it dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, Chinese five-spice powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt.
Add the lamb shoulder to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Remove the lamb shoulder from the marinade and place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Roast the lamb in the preheated oven for 2 hours, or until it reaches an internal temperature of 70°C.
While the lamb is roasting, prepare the bao by cutting the tortillas into 12 cm squares.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over low heat.
Once the lamb is cooked, remove it from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Using two forks, pull the lamb apart into shreds.
To assemble the bao, place a few tablespoons of the shredded lamb onto the center of a tortilla square.
Place a mozzarella cheese slice on top of the lamb.
Add a few green onions on top of the cheese.
Fold the bottom half of the tortilla up over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll up the bao to form a cylinder.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients to make 12 bao.
